Looking toward the 2050s under a high emissions scenario, the best climate match for your field is Walla Walla County, WA, which has a strong match quality with 8 out of 8 climate models in agreement. Lower sigma means a place's climate today is closer to your farm's future climate. 

Zero matching areas currently use your field's current rotation of Winter wheat to Barley to Pulses. The rotations used at the matching places include Winter wheat to Pulses, Winter wheat to Spring wheat to Pulses, and a flexible mix of pulses, spring wheat, and winter wheat.

Comparing your field to the best match today, your field has 23 days above 32 degrees Celsius per year compared to 32 days at the match, and 155 frost-free days compared to 193 days at the match. For afternoon ground temperature in June, your field is 37.0 degrees Celsius while the match is 31.9 degrees Celsius; for July-August afternoon ground temperature, which is mostly after harvest, your field is 40.3 degrees Celsius while the match is 43.3 degrees Celsius. In September, the driest-month soil water is 18.9 percent for your field and 17.8 percent for the match.

Overall, the future climate brings warmer temperatures and changes in precipitation across the year. These findings are based on 3351 farmland cells at approximately 4 kilometer resolution using the Cropland Data Layer.
